slot.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slot.brief: Plane electromagnetic wave of given intensity strikes a surface that is perfectly reflecting or perfectly absorbing; find the radiation pressure or force on the surface, comparing the two cases.

stem: A plane electromagnetic wave of intensity $1.2\times10^3\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ is incident normally on a surface of area $0.50\ \text{m}^2$. Find the difference between the forces when the surface is perfectly reflecting and perfectly absorbing. Take $c=3.0\times10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: For absorption, F = IA/c; for perfect reflection, F = 2IA/c. Their difference is IA/c = (1.2×10³)(0.50)/(3.0×10⁸) = 2.0×10⁻⁶ N.

working:
$F_{\text{abs}}=\dfrac{IA}{c}$; $F_{\text{refl}}=\dfrac{2IA}{c}$.
$F_{\text{refl}}-F_{\text{abs}}=\dfrac{IA}{c}$.
$=\dfrac{(1.2\times10^3)(0.50)}{3.0\times10^8}=2.0\times10^{-6}\ \text{N}$

Independent check: For absorption, F = IA/c; for perfect reflection, F = 2IA/c. Their difference is IA/c = (1.2×10³)(0.50)/(3.0×10⁸) = 2.0×10⁻⁶ N.
solution:
For absorption, $F_{\text{abs}}=IA/c$; for perfect reflection, $F_{\text{refl}}=2IA/c$. Thus,
$$F_{\text{refl}}-F_{\text{abs}}=\frac{IA}{c}=\frac{(1.2\times10^3)(0.50)}{3.0\times10^8}=2.0\times10^{-6}\ \text{N}$$
